designFeedback.findingTitle: Drill-Down Detail Exposure (Progressive Disclosure via Expandable Task Cells)
designFeedback.findingDescription: Essential data presented first with supporting metrics accessible via progressive drill-down that starts with a general overview and then goes into detail, facilitating data prioritization and creating clarity. For Mission Control's daily todos, each task cell shows only rank + title by default; tapping/clicking expands to reveal subtasks, due time, tags, or notes in a bottom-drawer slide or inline toggle. designFeedback.findingTitle: Streak Confetti Burst on Daily Completion
designFeedback.findingDescription: When the user checks off their first task of the day, trigger a brief 1-second CSS keyframe confetti animation (3–5 particles scaling and fading upward) centered on the streak badge in the header. The effect rewards daily habit closure with instant tactile feedback, reinforcing the JRPG battle-menu aesthetic while borrowing gamification momentum from modern habit trackers. Confetti only fires once per calendar day, preventing fatigue.

designFeedback.findingTitle: Anchor + Supporting Cell Ratio (Bento Hierarchy via Area, Not Just Label)
designFeedback.findingDescription: Every bento has one anchor that wins on size by a clear margin, ideally twice the area of the next cell, and the anchor is where the strongest copy, most important visual, or highest-stakes interaction lives. For Mission Control's daily todos, make the S-rank task an anchor (spanning 2 grid columns + 2 rows), A-ranks as secondary cells (1 col × 1.5 rows), and C-rank routine items as minimal supporting cells (1 col × 0.8 rows). Apps like Finch use a cozy, supportive interface for tracking daily goals, making productivity feel gentle rather than demanding. Add a floating "log today" button or a prominent quick-tap region at the bottom of the daily todo list that pre-fills today's date and opens a minimal modal (rank + title only). The best habit tracking apps offer a seamless habits setup process, making sure users log habits fast, reducing friction vs. the current three-step add flow.

designFeedback.findingTitle: Streaks with Confetti Micro-Animation on Daily Mark
designFeedback.findingDescription: Subtle micro animations and visual feedback like confetti explosions reward user actions in real-time. Mission Control has a static streak counter. Add a brief 1-second confetti burst (via CSS keyframes) when a user checks off today's first/final task, triggering only on the streak badge itself. Habit trackers now commonly feature confetti animations and Android support, and retro JRPG menus pair well with particle effects.

designFeedback.findingTitle: Difficulty Signaling via Visual Layering (Bento Grid Weight)
designFeedback.findingDescription: Bento grid is an information architecture decision that controls cognitive load by giving each piece of data its own spatial weight. Apply this to daily todos: bigger/taller cards for high-rank (S/A) tasks, compact rows for routine (C) ones. This mirrors how a hero tile spanning 6 columns creates visual hierarchy through spatial weight so the bigger tile appears more important—letting users visually triage at a glance without text labels.

designFeedback.findingTitle: Immediate Visual Feedback on Task Completion
designFeedback.findingDescription: The core of the experience is the visual feedback loop. When a user marks a habit as complete, the app must acknowledge it—instantly and satisfyingly. This doesn't mean over-the-top fireworks, but a clear, immediate confirmation that their effort has been recorded. Mission Control already does this well with XP pop animations; enhancing it with a color pulse or rank-check notification (e.g., "S-rank locked" at task completion) would deepen the JRPG feel.

Streak forgiveness (freezes, grace days, pause buttons) went from premium feature to baseline expectation, driven by the fact that an unforgiving streak breaks once and then breaks forever, because the psychological cost of restarting from zero is heavier than the cost of skipping today. Mission Control could let players "freeze" one day per week without losing their XP streak, or offer a monthly streak-reset token—keeping the JRPG rank feel while staying psychologically forgiving.

thread-1786428178060-1-streaks-with-conf.title: Consequential Instant Feedback: Haptic + Audio Pulse on Task Completion
thread-1786428178060-1-streaks-with-conf.description: Tapping a habit gives instant XP and gold feedback, making choices feel consequential. Instead of a silent animation, Mission Control's checkbox could trigger a brief haptic pulse (vibration on mobile, rumble on controller-paired desktops) paired with a subtle chime—creating a tactile, multi-sensory reward loop that feels *earned* rather than decorative. The sensation is instantaneous and dismissible, respecting focus while confirming the action unmistakably.

thread-1786428178060-2-tap-to-log-quick-.title: Partial-Fill Progress Bar (Done/Do Habits Pattern)
thread-1786428178060-2-tap-to-log-quick-.description: Done's minimalist habit tracker uses a single-tap interface where gray habit bars fill with color as you progress toward a daily goal—no navigation, no forms, no friction. Apply this to Mission Control's todo list by replacing checkboxes with color-coded progress bars for today's todos; tapping a bar increments its fill and triggers instant XP feedback, turning logging into satisfying micro-interactions that keep streaks alive.
